legend: A permutation is a sequence of length n$$$n$$$ consisting of integers from 1$$$1$$$ to n$$$n$$$, in which all the numbers occur exactly once. For example, [1]$$$[1]$$$, [3,5,2,1,4]$$$[3,5,2,1,4]$$$, and [1,3,2]$$$[1,3,2]$$$ are permutations, whereas [2,3,2]$$$[2,3,2]$$$, [4,3,1]$$$[4,3,1]$$$, and [0]$$$[0]$$$ are not.

You are given an array A1,A2,…,AN$$$A_1, A_2, \dots, A_N$$$ consisting of N$$$N$$$ integers. Each integer is 0$$$0$$$ or 1$$$1$$$. Find the number of permutations P$$$P$$$ of size N$$$N$$$ such that the following conditions hold:
APi≡i(mod2)$$$A_{P_i} \equiv i \pmod{2}$$$, for all (1≤i≤N$$$1 \leq i \leq N$$$).
Because the number of such permutations can be very large, print the answer modulo 998244353$$$998244353$$$.
input: The first line contains an integer N (1≤N≤106)$$$N \ (1 \leq N \leq 10^6)$$$.
The second line contains N$$$N$$$ space separated integers Ai$$$A_i$$$ - the elements of the array. It's guaranteed that Ai∈{0,1}$$$A_i \in \{0, 1\}$$$.
output: Output a single line containing the number of permutations satisfying the conditions modulo 998244353$$$998244353$$$.
